title: On the Dewy Breath of Even
description: On the Dewy Breath of Even in Tonic Solfa to GALILEE (JUDE), doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 554, “Evening Hymn”, where the book credits them to Martineau's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GALILEE (JUDE); any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: On the dew-y breath of e-ven Thou-sand o-dors min-gling rise, Borne like in-cense up to hea-ven, Na-ture's eve-ning sac-ri-fice.

lines: On the dewy breath of even
Borne like incense up to heaven, —
To Thy throne, O Lord, ascending, —
Incense of our hearts to Thee.
All our days with gladness bless,
Let Thine eye, that knows no slumber,
Then, though conscious we are sleeping
In the outer courts of death,
Calm we rest in perfect faith.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to GALILEE (JUDE) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
